what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: An outreach agent mapped eleven companies that control AI agents at Web Summit, in their own words; most are partners as much as competitors.
sections.para: The Web Summit team's outreach agent and two research agents read eleven companies' sites on 5 November and built a public page: a map, a before-during-after chain, each company's headline and offer with its source and attendance label, where RiskMandate differs, where it is behind, and seven things to do before 12 November. Almost everyone works while or after the agent acts; RiskMandate works before, so their products are barriers a policy can name. The newsroom checked it; small corrections are listed.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Eleven companies, one public page, before versus during and after, partners as much as competitors, honest gaps, checked.
sections.para: Six points from the page and the newsroom's check of it.

sections.label: What the page is
sections.line: A team member's ask, answered by 23:10 UTC with a page built from each company's own words.
sections.para: Headline, offer and call to action from each site with the link; attendance labelled by how it is known; RiskMandate's view marked as its own; a public version without judgements and a private fuller one.

sections.label: Before, during, after
sections.line: RiskMandate acts before the agent does; seven companies act while it acts and three after.
sections.para: A tool-call gate, a payment account with caps or scopes from an identity provider are barriers, and a signed receipt is evidence, that an Agent Behaviour Policy can name.

sections.label: The eleven, in one line each
sections.line: Each company in one line, with where RiskMandate differs.
sections.para: Summit Cognitive and Airia closest; Hexgate, Polygraf AI, Conscium, Delinea and Arsia Labs overlap in part; Descope, Keyban, Forg3t and TrustScale are neighbours.

sections.label: Where we are behind, and what to do about it
sections.line: Six ways RiskMandate is behind, and seven things to do before the stand on 12 November.
sections.para: No customer names, no headline number, the sample policy not first, no booking link, a long hook, no 'free, no card'; the fixes include one number on the stand and a joint before-during-after demo.

sections.label: What the newsroom checked
sections.line: Nine of eleven headlines match on the cited page; the corrections are small.
sections.para: Delinea's headline is on its home page, Keyban's cited page is French, Polygraf's site refused our reader, Summit Cognitive's pilot is $25,000, Descope does not say per-agent scopes. Attendance is the softest part.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: Placements and differences are RiskMandate's view; attendance is as labelled.
sections.para: No judgement of the companies; team members are not named.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: The team's competitive page and data file, its company map, and each company's own site.
